+-- | The closed MinBars resolver: the fixed helper names map to their helpers; an
+-- | unknown name (which the desugar never emits) throws `HelperError`.
+minResolve :: forall m. MonadThrow Error m => MinEnv -> String -> m (Operation m MinEnv)
+minResolve _ name = case name of
+  "mlookup" -> pure mlookupH
+  "escape" -> pure escapeH
+  "section" -> pure sectionH
+  "inverted" -> pure invertedH
+  "partial" -> pure partialH
+  "parent" -> pure parentH
+  "block" -> pure blockH
+  other -> throwError (HelperError ("unknown MinBars helper '" <> other <> "'"))
+

 -- | (parent fallback), per `MinBars.Context.mresolve`. The name is baked in by

 Core:        {{{{raw}}}}Hello {{name}}{{{{/raw}}}}   (verbatim; `raw` engine helper returns body)
 ```
 
+:::note
+*A raw block's head resolves **strictly**.* A raw block exists only to hand its
+verbatim body to a helper (via `options.fn()`), so its head must name a defined
+operation — an undefined head is a hard `UnknownHelper` error in **every** dialect,
+never an implicit section. (This is why the worked example uses `raw`, the engine's
+identity passthrough helper, and the MaxBars/FullBars references register their own
+`rawloud`/`raw-loud`.) FullBars therefore diverges from Handlebars' `blockHelperMissing`
+here: there is no silent fall-through to a context section for a raw block. The common
+`{{{{raw}}}}…{{{{/raw}}}}` keeps working because `raw` is a prelude helper.
+:::
+
 :::note
 *Standalone whitespace.* Like Handlebars, FlatBars removes a line that holds only a standalone block
 open/close or a comment, so a control tag leaves no blank line. This is **on by default** and runs as

{t("{{x}}")} HTML-escapes; the triple-stash {t("{{{x}}}")} emits raw markup — unchanged from FullBars.

+

Raw blocks

+

+ A raw block — four staches, {t("{{{{#op}}}}…{{{{/op}}}}")} (MaxBars + uses the # sigil, like RawBars) — hands its body to the operation + unprocessed: the inner {t("{{bar}}")} is never interpreted, + it's literal text the operation receives via options.fn(). Useful + when a template must emit mustache syntax it should not expand (docs, + code samples). Here rawloud upper-cases the raw body, so the verbatim + {t("{{bar}}")} comes out as {t("{{BAR}}")}. The head + must name a defined operation — a raw block exists only to feed one, so an + undefined head is a hard error, never a silent empty render. +
